High-level answers:
- SAST: We run CodeQL + custom rules in CI for every PR; full repo baseline scans nightly. Findings triaged by engineering triage board; high-severity results (S0/S1) are acknowledged within 24-48 hours and assigned an owner. We also run pre-merge checks to block PRs with critical/high secrets or crypto misuse.
- DAST: Weekly DAST on staging, with continuous lightweight active scanning in pre-prod. For customer-facing hosted endpoints we run quarterly manual validation and targeted fuzzing during release windows. DAST tooling includes a mix of in-house harnesses and vendor scanners (commercial scanners + open-source).
- Patch SLAs (initial): Critical/P1 (publicly disclosed, exploitable) — initial mitigation or compensating controls within 24 hours; remediation patch planned and scheduled within 7 business days for Dedicated/Private customers under contract. For our hosted shared service we aim for mitigation within 24 hours and patch rollout within 14 calendar days depending on impact and coordinated rollback plans; we can formalize a tighter SLA in a Dedicated addendum.
- Pen tests: Annual third-party pentest + targeted scopes before major releases. Executive summaries are provided to customers under NDA; full reports are supplied under MSA/controlled distribution.
- SBOM: Generated per image and exported in CycloneDX/CSV. We can provide signed SBOM extracts and maintain weekly updates for per-customer Dedicated or on-prem deployments.

Ellen — quick technical follow-up on the patching and DAST process:

- Patching workflow: Triage (S0/S1) -> Emergency fix branch -> Canary rollout -> Full rollout. For Dedicated/Private customers with reserved capacity we prioritize builds/patch channels and provide hotfix backports. Canary windows are typically 1-2 hours for infra-level changes, with expanded rollout after smoke checks (latency/error metrics).
- Mitigation vs patch: We distinguish immediate mitigations (WAF rules, ACL changes, config toggles) from code patches. We document compensating controls in the ticket and communicate ETA to affected customers.
- DAST methodology: Staging full-scan weekly; runtime instrumentation used to reduce false positives; findings are triaged with reproducible PoC. For public endpoints we also run automated scheduled scans more frequently (lightweight weekly) and escalate high-severity VULN findings to the on-call SRE.
- Third-party dependencies: We operate a dependency-monitoring pipeline (OSS scanners + vendor feeds) that raises alerts for new CVEs. For packages flagged as high-risk we create a dedicated remediation ticket with an ETA and owner.

If HydroCore needs exact wording for an SLA table (e.g., P1 mitigation within X hours, full patch within Y days) we can propose formal language and include it in a security appendix.
